messages.content: coordinator joined the conversation

@[[7149ae7b-ab12-4e53-acc4-ebfd10d4cf5e]] Build all four stages of this job end to end with the band, without asking me anything. Work the stages in order, pipelined as your instructions describe: the next stage starts once the reviewer and the customer have accepted the current one, and every stage must still close with all four verifiers’ accepts.

Kickoff package (specs and shipped checks): /Users/kosesena/Desktop/dark-factory/dark-factory-wearedevs
Track: tablekeeper
Specifications: /Users/kosesena/Desktop/dark-factory/dark-factory-wearedevs/tablekeeper/spec/stage-1.md through stage-4.md (read each in full; paste the full text of the current stage into every handoff; every earlier stage's requirements continue to apply).
Shipped checks (partial, read-only; never build to them; run them only through the check command): /Users/kosesena/Desktop/dark-factory/dark-factory-wearedevs/tablekeeper/test/stage_1/ through stage_4/
Result repository (absolute path, commit here, every file the band produces goes inside it): /Users/kosesena/Desktop/dark-factory/band-work/tablekeeper-run
Stage folders: /Users/kosesena/Desktop/dark-factory/band-work/tablekeeper-run/stage-1/ through stage-4/. Each is a complete service with its own Dockerfile and RUN.md; stage N+1 starts as a copy of the accepted stage N, carried forward and extended. Stage folders contain no .git.

Run contract (from spec sections 2-3; it applies to every stage):
- Deliver a Dockerfile and a RUN.md per stage folder. The harness builds the image, runs it with -e PORT=<port> and a port mapping, and tests only HTTP behaviour. Single container, no compose.
- Listen on 0.0.0.0:$PORT (default 8080). GET /health returns 200 {"status":"ok"} within 60 s of container start.
- POST /_test/reset replaces all state with the fixture in the body and returns 204; it stays enabled and unauthenticated in the delivered image.
- No outbound network at run time (only during docker build). Limits: 2 vCPU, 2 GiB, up to 50 requests in flight, 5 s per request (10 s for reset).

Check command (run from the kickoff package directory; use a new --out name every time; replace N with the stage):
cd /Users/kosesena/Desktop/dark-factory/dark-factory-wearedevs && . .venv/bin/activate && python -m harness run --track tablekeeper --repo /Users/kosesena/Desktop/dark-factory/band-work/tablekeeper-run --stage N --out /Users/kosesena/Desktop/dark-factory/band-work/checks/tk-<new-unique-name>
The final check of each stage must also pass with --mode isolated added.

Tools: Docker is at /usr/local/bin/docker. A headless browser (Playwright with Chromium) is installed in the kickoff package's .venv: activate it as in the check command and drive it from Python.

Done means, for each stage: the isolated check prints "claimed stage: N"; the spec-auditor has no open gaps that cite a specification sentence and has reported its fault-seeding results; the reviewer has accepted the committed revision; the customer has accepted it (from stage 2: screens at desktop and phone widths, screenshots committed in the result repository); the cross-auditor has accepted it. A stage is closed only with all four accepts on the same revision. Then report back here once, covering all four stages, with the measurement table your instructions ask for.

=== FULL SPECIFICATION, STAGE 1 ===
# Tablekeeper — Stage 1: reservations

This stage defines the initial service and its API.

Build from the supplied requirements. Source code, API documentation and schemas from
existing products in this domain must not be used.

## 1. Scope

Diners can search restaurant availability, book a table and receive a confirmation
reference. They can cancel or amend their bookings, including changing several bookings
together. Each restaurant has its own table capacities, opening hours and cancellation policy.
Only the HTTP API is required.

Two `confirmed` reservations must never occupy the same table at overlapping times,
including during concurrent requests. Occupancy is the half-open interval
`[starts_at, starts_at + reservation_duration)`. A 90-minute booking at 19:00 therefore
does not overlap a booking starting at 20:30. Retries and rejected requests must not
create duplicate or partial bookings.

## 2. Delivery and deployment

Deliver an HTTP service, a `Dockerfile` and a `RUN.md` with a command that builds and
starts the service without manual setup. Language, framework and storage are unrestricted.
A `docker-compose.yml` is optional.

The submission is a containerized HTTP service, not a Python package. Python is not
required in the implementation. TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java, Python and any
other language are equally valid. The harness builds the submitted `Dockerfile`, starts
the resulting image and tests only its HTTP behavior; it does not import or execute the
submission's source files on the judge host.

The image must run on its own with `-e PORT=<port>` and a port mapping. Runtime networking
has no outbound access. All runtime dependencies, initialization and seed data must work
within that single container. Compose configuration is not used to start the service.

### Resource limits

The service must operate within these limits:

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 2 vCPU |
| Memory | 2 GiB |
| Start to first healthy response | 60 s |
| Concurrent requests | up to 50 in flight |
| Per-request timeout | 5 s (10 s for `POST /_test/reset`) |
| Outbound network | available during `docker build`, **none at run time** |
| Disk | ephemeral; state need not survive a container restart |

Runtime assets and dependencies must be included in the image. This includes fonts,
scripts and stylesheets; external services are unavailable at runtime.

## 3. Runtime contract

### 3.1 Listening

Listen on `0.0.0.0` using the `PORT` environment variable, default `8080`.

### 3.2 Health

```http
GET /health  ->  200  {"status": "ok"}
```

Return 200 once the service and its data store can serve requests, within 60 seconds
of container start. Non-200 responses are permitted before the service is ready.

### 3.3 Reset and seed

```http
POST /_test/reset
Content-Type: application/json

{ ...fixture... }

->  204 No Content
```

Replace all service state with the fixture in the request body (§4). When reset returns
204, subsequent requests must see only that fixture. Repeated resets are supported.
This test endpoint must be enabled in the delivered image and requires no authentication.

### 3.4 Conventions

- Requests and responses are `application/json; charset=utf-8`.
- Timestamps in responses are RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, e.g. `2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00`.
- Unknown fields in a request body are ignored, never an error.
- Unknown query parameters are ignored.
- IDs are opaque strings of at most 64 characters. Their format is yours. This limit
  also applies to IDs supplied in reset fixtures.

## 4. Model

Restaurants and tables are supplied through `POST /_test/reset` only. Restaurant and
table creation endpoints are out of scope.

| Field | On | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `timezone` | Restaurant | IANA zone name, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. All of the restaurant's times are local to this |
| `slot_minutes` | Restaurant | Bookings start on a grid of this many minutes from opening time |
| `reservation_duration_minutes` | Restaurant | How long every reservation occupies its table |
| `cancellation_cutoff_minutes` | Restaurant | A booking cannot be cancelled or changed within this many minutes of its start |
| `opening_hours` | Restaurant | Per weekday. A day with no entry is closed |
| `capacity` | Table | Maximum party size |

### Fixture format

```json
{
  "users": [
    { "id": "u_ada", "email": "ada@example.com",
      "password": "correct horse", "display_name": "Ada" }
  ],
  "restaurants": [
    {
      "id": "r_anker",
      "name": "Zum Anker",
      "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
      "slot_minutes": 30,
      "reservation_duration_minutes": 90,
      "cancellation_cutoff_minutes": 120,
      "opening_hours": [
        { "weekday": "thu", "opens": "18:00", "closes": "23:00" },
        { "weekday": "fri", "opens": "18:00", "closes": "23:30" }
      ],
      "tables": [
        { "id": "t_1", "label": "1", "capacity": 2 },
        { "id": "t_2", "label": "2", "capacity": 4 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "reservations": []
}
```

- `weekday` is one of `mon tue wed thu fri sat sun`.
- `opens` and `closes` are local `HH:MM`, 24-hour. `closes` is always later than `opens` on the
  same local day — opening hours never cross midnight.
- Seeded users must be able to log in with the given password immediately.
- `reservations` may seed confirmed bookings, with the same fields as a `POST /reservations`
  body plus `id`, `reference` and `user_id`.

Fixtures may use any calendar date. A booking must not be rejected solely because its
start is in the past; the cancellation and amendment cutoff rules still apply.

## 5. Errors

Every 4xx and 5xx response carries this body:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "table_unavailable", "message": "human readable, any wording" } }
```

Use the specified HTTP status and `code`. The human-readable `message` may use any wording.
Endpoint-specific errors are listed with each endpoint.

| Status | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `malformed_request` | Unparseable body, or a field of the wrong JSON type |
| 400 | `missing_idempotency_key` | Required `Idempotency-Key` header absent or empty |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token |
| 403 | `forbidden` | Authenticated, but not permitted to touch this resource |
| 404 | `not_found` | No such resource, or not visible to this caller |
| 409 | `idempotency_key_reuse` | Key already used by this caller with a different request body |
| 422 | `validation_failed` | A required field or query parameter is missing, or a stated rule is violated with no more specific code |

A field of the correct JSON type with an invalid format or out-of-range value gives
422 `validation_failed`, unless an endpoint specifies a different error. This includes
invalid dates, negative counts and values exceeding a stated maximum or length. In addition:

- Endpoint-specific field rules take precedence: invalid `party_size` values (including strings
  and booleans) and `starts_at_local` strings that are not a bare local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` are
  422 `validation_failed`. Other wrong JSON types follow the rule below.
- An integer-valued **query parameter** is written as plain decimal digits: `1e9`, `4.0` and `+4`
  are 422 `validation_failed` whatever their numeric value.
- Reserve 400 `malformed_request` for a body that does not parse or a field of the wrong type.

Shared ranges, enforced on every endpoint that takes them:

| Field | Valid | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | 1 to 255 characters | 422 `validation_failed` |

Requests must not produce 5xx responses, including under concurrent load.

## 6. Authentication

Authentication supports signup and login. Email verification, password reset, refresh
tokens and role-management endpoints are out of scope. Permissions specified elsewhere
in these requirements still apply.

```http
POST /auth/signup
{ "email": "a@example.com", "password": "correct horse", "display_name": "Ada" }

->  201  { "user_id": "u_1", "display_name": "Ada", "token": "..." }
```

```http
POST /auth/login
{ "email": "a@example.com", "password": "correct horse" }

->  200  { "user_id": "u_1", "display_name": "Ada", "token": "..." }
```

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| Email already registered | 409 `email_taken` |
| Password shorter than 8 characters | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `email` not of the form `local@domain` | 422 `validation_failed` |
| Wrong password or unknown email on login | 401 `unauthenticated` |

Every other endpoint requires a bearer token, except `/health`, `/_test/reset`, the two above, and
the three public endpoints named at the top of §8 — `GET /restaurants`, `GET /restaurants/{id}` and
`GET /availability`:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Tokens do not expire. An account may have multiple valid tokens and concurrent sessions.

Passwords must be stored using a password-hashing function such as bcrypt, scrypt or
Argon2, or an equivalent. Plaintext password storage is not permitted.

## 7. Idempotency

Two write paths require an idempotency key: **`POST /reservations`** (§8) and
**`POST /reservation-moves`** (§11).

```http
Idempotency-Key: <client-chosen string, 1..255 characters>
```

The key is scoped to **the authenticated user**. Two different users may use the same key string
with no interaction between them.

A replay means the same user sending the **same method, the same path and the same body**. The
same key with the same body on a different path is a different request, not a replay, and must
succeed normally.

After the body has been parsed as a JSON object and the caller authenticated, idempotency
is resolved before endpoint-specific field validation or current-resource checks. Thus a
used key with a different JSON body returns `409 idempotency_key_reuse` even when that new
body would otherwise be invalid.

| Situation | Response |
|---|---|
| Header absent or empty | 400 `missing_idempotency_key` |
| First use of the key | The normal response, **201** |
| Replay: same key, same body | **200**, body identical to the original response as a JSON value |
| Same key, different body | 409 `idempotency_key_reuse` |
| Key reused after the original request failed with 4xx | Treated as a first use |

"Same body" means the same JSON value after parsing — key order and whitespace do not matter.

For concurrent identical requests with an unused key, exactly one returns 201.
The others return 200 with the same body. The operation takes effect only once.

A successful replay returns the original response, even after the resource changes or
is cancelled. It makes no further state changes.

## 8. API

`GET /restaurants`, `GET /restaurants/{id}` and `GET /availability` are **public** — no bearer
token. Everything else needs one. Diners browse before they sign in.

### `GET /restaurants`

```json
{ "restaurants": [ { "id": "r_anker", "name": "Zum Anker", "timezone": "Europe/Berlin" } ] }
```

### `GET /restaurants/{id}`

The restaurant with its `slot_minutes`, `reservation_duration_minutes`,
`cancellation_cutoff_minutes`, `opening_hours` and `tables`, in the fixture's shape. 404 if
unknown.

### `GET /availability`

```http
GET /availability?restaurant_id=r_anker&date=2026-09-24&party_size=4
```

All three parameters are required; a missing one is 422 `validation_failed`. `date` is a local
calendar date at the restaurant.

```json
{
  "restaurant_id": "r_anker",
  "date": "2026-09-24",
  "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
  "slots": [
    { "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T18:00",
      "starts_at": "2026-09-24T18:00:00+02:00",
      "available_table_ids": ["t_2"] }
  ]
}
```

`starts_at_local` is the full `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` and goes into `POST /reservations` unchanged.

A slot appears for every `slot_minutes` step from `opens` such that
`slot + reservation_duration_minutes <= closes`. `available_table_ids` lists the tables of that
restaurant with `capacity >= party_size` and no overlapping confirmed reservation, in fixture
order. A slot with no available table still appears, with an empty list.

A closed day returns `"slots": []`.

### `POST /reservations`

`Idempotency-Key` is required; see §7.

```http
POST /reservations
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: 2f9c1a...

{ "restaurant_id": "r_anker", "table_id": "t_2",
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00", "party_size": 4 }
```

`starts_at_local` is wall-clock at the restaurant, with no offset and no `Z`. Resolve it against
the restaurant's `timezone`.

```json
201
{
  "reservation_id": "res_7",
  "reference": "K3P7QW",
  "restaurant_id": "r_anker",
  "table_id": "t_2",
  "party_size": 4,
  "status": "confirmed",
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00",
  "starts_at": "2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00",
  "ends_at": "2026-09-24T20:30:00+02:00",
  "created_at": "2026-09-21T11:04:03+00:00"
}
```

`reference` is 6 to 12 characters of `A-Z0-9`, unique across all reservations, and never changes.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| The table is taken for an overlapping interval | 409 `table_unavailable` |
| `starts_at_local` is not on the slot grid | 422 `not_on_slot_grid` |
| Slot outside opening hours, or the reservation would end after `closes` | 422 `outside_opening_hours` |
| `party_size` exceeds the table's `capacity` | 422 `party_exceeds_capacity` |
| `party_size` below 1, or not an integer | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `starts_at_local` is a local time that does not exist (see §9) | 422 `invalid_local_time` |
| Unknown restaurant, unknown table, or the table belongs to another restaurant | 404 `not_found` |

### `GET /reservations`

The caller's reservations, `starts_at` descending, confirmed and cancelled alike.
Return `200` with `{"reservations": [...]}`; each entry has the same shape as the
create response. An empty list is `{"reservations": []}`.

### `GET /reservations/{reference}`

One reservation. **404 if it is not the caller's** — do not leak the existence of other people's
bookings.

### `POST /reservations/{reference}/cancel`

```json
200
{ "reference": "K3P7QW", "status": "cancelled", ... }
```

Frees the table immediately: the next `GET /availability` must offer that slot again.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| Already cancelled | 200 with the current state — cancelling twice is not an error |
| Now is within `cancellation_cutoff_minutes` of `starts_at`, or later | 409 `cutoff_passed` |
| Not the caller's reservation | 404 `not_found` |

### `PATCH /reservations/{reference}`

Change the time, the table or the party size. Any subset of `table_id`, `starts_at_local`,
`party_size`. No idempotency key is required here.

Validation is identical to `POST /reservations`, and the same cutoff rule as cancel applies
(409 `cutoff_passed`), measured against the **current** start time. A cancelled reservation is
409 `reservation_cancelled`. A successful amendment releases the old slot and reserves the
new one together. A failed amendment leaves the original booking and its occupancy unchanged.

`reference` and `reservation_id` survive a change.

## 9. Time and DST

Local dates and times follow the restaurant's `timezone`, including daylight-saving transitions.

**Spring forward.** Local times in the skipped hour do not exist. They never appear in
availability, and booking one is 422 `invalid_local_time`.

**Fall back.** Local times in the repeated hour occur twice. **Always resolve to the first
occurrence — the one before the clocks change.** The slot appears once in availability, and the
second occurrence is not bookable.

`reservation_duration_minutes` is **absolute time**, not wall-clock. A 90-minute reservation
starting at 01:30 on a fall-back night ends 90 real minutes later, and its local `ends_at` will
read 02:00, not 03:00.

The transitions that must be handled:

| Zone | Spring forward | Fall back |
|---|---|---|
| `Europe/Berlin` | 2026-03-29, 02:00 → 03:00 | 2026-10-25, 03:00 → 02:00 |
| `America/New_York` | 2026-03-08, 02:00 → 03:00 | 2026-11-01, 02:00 → 01:00 |

Offsets must follow the IANA rules for the specified zone and date.

## 10. Export and import

The service must support `GET /_test/export` and `POST /_test/import`. Like reset, these
are unauthenticated test endpoints.
Exports may contain credentials and session tokens; handle them as private test artifacts.
Return 200 from export with a JSON object containing `track: "tablekeeper"`,
`format_version: 1` and `state` (an implementation-defined JSON object). The state format
is opaque to the caller and must be accepted unchanged by import.

Import takes that entire object and atomically replaces the service's state, returning
204. It must accept an unchanged export produced by this service. No dependency on the
source process, files, volume, port or network address is allowed. Import is replacement,
not merge; repeating it restores the exported state without duplicating anything. Invalid
JSON follows §5; missing fields, wrong track/version or an invalid state give 422
`validation_failed` without changing the destination. Test control calls have a 10-second
timeout. Export is an atomic, read-only snapshot; subsequent source writes do not change it.

Preserve accounts and hashed-password login, existing bearer tokens, fixture configuration,
reservations, references, all completed idempotent request bodies and original responses.
Identities, statuses and timestamps must not be regenerated. Failed request keys remain
reusable. Existing receipts, references, tokens and retries must remain valid after import;
replacing the state with a fresh fixture does not satisfy this requirement. Import removes
all previous destination data and credentials. Reset continues to clear all state, including
imported state. State need not survive an abrupt container restart.

## 11. Atomic reservation moves

A diner may change several bookings in one request.

`POST /reservation-moves` requires authentication and an idempotency key. Body:

```json
{"moves": [{"reference": "BOOK01", "table_id": "t_2"},
           {"reference": "BOOK02", "table_id": "t_1"}]}
```

`moves` contains 1..8 objects with distinct string references. Invalid shape or duplicate
references gives 422 `validation_failed`. Every booking must belong to the caller and the
same restaurant. Unknown/another owner's reference gives 404 `not_found`; different
restaurants give 422 `validation_failed`. No token gives 401.

Each item accepts the ordinary PATCH fields `table_id`, `starts_at_local`, `party_size`;
omitted fields retain their current values and unknown fields are ignored. The booking's
identity, owner and creation time never change. Cancelled bookings give 409
`reservation_cancelled`. Each booking's existing cutoff applies. Non-occupancy errors use
ordinary amendment codes and take precedence in input order, with cutoff errors preceding
other changes for that booking. An overlap among resulting bookings or with an unlisted
booking gives 409 `table_unavailable`. Unchanged listed bookings retain their occupancy.

Either every move commits or nothing changes: occupancy, reservation records and retry
keys. On success return 201 with `{"reservations": [...]}` in input order, including
unchanged items.
Replays return that original response with 200, even after amendments or cancellations.
No-op moves retain all existing values. Export/import preserves successful batch receipts
as well as the resulting bookings. No batch UI is required.

The stage 1 audit is finished and committed as `24c392a` in `band-work/tablekeeper-run`. I wrote no product code.

- **Requirements ledger** (`audit/ledger-stage-1.md`): 136 numbered requirements, each quoting its spec sentence and section and marked covered, partly covered or uncovered against the shipped checks. Roughly a third falls in each group. It also lists 10 ambiguities, each with the reading I'd take and why.
- **Gap list** (`audit/gaps-stage-1.md`): 51 items ranked by how likely an implementation is to get them wrong. Each one has the quote, what a violation looks like and a scenario to test it.
- **Pointer file** (`ledger/stage-1.md`): points to the two files above, since my seat brief asks for a `ledger/` folder.

The shipped checks barely touch three areas:
- **Batch moves:** only a single-item move is checked. The spec's own swap example (two bookings trading tables), overlap detection and all-or-nothing behaviour are never exercised.
- **Export/import:** only one booking restore is checked. Retries surviving an import, rejection of a bad import, and import replacing rather than merging are never exercised.
- **Concurrency:** only 10 simultaneous creates on one slot are checked. Same-key races, edit races and 50 requests in flight are not.

The highest-risk single gaps are:
- An edit moving a booking to an overlapping time on the same table wrongly conflicting with itself.
- An idempotency key being judged reused before the request body is validated.
- A key from a failed request not being reusable.
- Past dates being refused.
- Daylight-saving bugs: skipped times appearing in availability, and overlap on the night the clocks go back being compared by local time rather than real time.
- Reservation IDs colliding after a seed or import.

@[[7149ae7b-ab12-4e53-acc4-ebfd10d4cf5e]] STAGE 1 AUDIT-FIRST is done. Commit 24c392a in tablekeeper-run.

- Ledger: audit/ledger-stage-1.md. It has 136 numbered requirements (R1–R136), each quoting the spec sentence it comes from with its § section, plus 10 ambiguities with proposed readings (A1–A10).
- Gap list: audit/gaps-stage-1.md, 51 ranked items. Pointer file: ledger/stage-1.md.
- Coverage: about 45 rows are fully covered by the shipped checks, about 45 partly and about 45 not at all. The shipped checks never test §11 moves beyond a single item. They don't test export/import beyond one restore, or concurrency beyond 10 creates on one slot.
- Gap list part 1/2 (tiers 1–2) is below. Part 2/2 (tier 3 and the ambiguities) follows as a separate message.

**TIER 1: very likely to be wrong**
1. **R95** "A successful amendment releases the old slot and reserves the new one together." PATCH 19:00 → 19:30 on the **same** table must return 200, not conflict with itself. Afterwards, 19:00 is free and the new interval is held.
2. **R130/R129** "An overlap among resulting bookings or with an unlisted booking gives 409 table_unavailable." The spec's own example is a swap.
   - A swap (A t_1→t_2, B t_2→t_1, same time) must return 201.
   - A batch putting two listed bookings on one table at overlapping times must return 409, and nothing changes.
   - Moving onto a table held by an unlisted booking must return 409.
3. **R132/R5/R96** "Either every move commits or nothing changes: occupancy, reservation records and retry keys." / "A failed amendment leaves the original booking and its occupancy unchanged."
   - A batch [valid A, B off-grid] must return 422, with A untouched and its old slot still blocked.
   - The same key with a corrected body must then return 201.
   - A PATCH onto a taken table must return 409, and the original slot stays occupied.
4. **R56** "a used key with a different JSON body returns 409 idempotency_key_reuse even when that new body would otherwise be invalid." Key K used once; then K with party_size 0 or an unknown restaurant must return 409, not 422 or 404.
5. **R60** "Key reused after the original request failed with 4xx: Treated as a first use." K on an off-grid time returns 422. K again with a valid *different* body must return 201.
6. **R62** "exactly one returns 201. The others return 200 with the same body. The operation takes effect only once." 20 parallel identical POSTs with one key must give one 201 and nineteen 200s with identical bodies. GET /reservations must then show exactly one booking.
7. **R2** "including during concurrent requests". With 50 in flight:
   - PATCHes of different bookings onto one free table: exactly one 200.
   - Cancel racing new creates on the freed slot: at most one confirmed booking.
   - Overlapping but non-identical starts (19:00 and 19:30) on one table: exactly one 201.
   - Concurrent move batches touching the same tables: the invariant holds.
8. **R28** "A booking must not be rejected solely because its start is in the past". POST a past on-grid booking must return 201. Cancelling or PATCHing it must return 409 cutoff_passed.
9. **R99** Skipped local times "never appear in availability". Berlin 2026-03-29 and New York 2026-03-08 (open 00:00–23:30) must show no 02:xx slot.
10. **R104** Overlap uses absolute instants. On Berlin 2026-10-25:
    - Book 01:30 on table B; it ends 02:00+01:00.
    - Book 02:00 (+02:00, first occurrence) on B: must return 409 table_unavailable.
11. **R20** "Bookings start on a grid of this many minutes from opening time". With opens 18:15, closes 22:00, slot 30, duration 90:
    - Slots must be 18:15, 18:45 … 20:15.
    - 20:30 must return 422 not_on_slot_grid.
12. **R119** IDs and references must stay "unique across all reservations" after a seed or import.
    - Seed a reservation with id res_1, then create one: it gets a different reservation_id and reference.
    - Export, create, import, create: no ID or reference collides.

**TIER 2: likely to be wrong**
13. **R114/R113** "Preserve ... all completed idempotent request bodies and original responses" plus login. Create with K, export, reset, import. Then:
    - K with the same body: 200 with the original body.
    - K with a different body: 409.
    - Password login: 200.
14. **R111** "missing fields, wrong track/version or an invalid state give 422 validation_failed without changing the destination".
    - `{}`, `track:"other"`, `format_version:2`, `state:"x"` each return 422, and the existing data is still readable.
    - `{bad` returns 400.
15. **R117/R118/R110** "Import removes all previous destination data and credentials" / "Reset continues to clear all state, including imported state" / "without duplicating anything".
    - A user signed up on the destination before import: token and login both give 401.
    - Importing the same snapshot twice does not duplicate anything.
    - A reset clears the imported state.
16. **R11** Reset must "Replace all service state". A user signed up before the reset must get 401 (token and login). An old key with the same body must give 201, not a replay.
17. **R120–R127** Move-batch validation. In every case, nothing changes.
    - 422 validation_failed: 0 or 9 moves, duplicate references, a non-string reference, bookings in two restaurants.
    - 404: another user's reference.
    - 409 reservation_cancelled: a cancelled booking.
    - 409 cutoff_passed: a booking inside its cutoff.
    - 401: no token. 400 missing_idempotency_key: no key.
    - 422 party_exceeds_capacity: a party over capacity.
18. **R128** "take precedence in input order, with cutoff errors preceding other changes for that booking".
    - [A off-grid, B cancelled] → 422 not_on_slot_grid.
    - [B cancelled, A off-grid] → 409 reservation_cancelled.
    - A inside its cutoff with an off-grid time → 409 cutoff_passed.
19. **R134/R125/R135/R133** Batch receipts.
    - A replay after cancelling a moved booking: 200 with the identical body.
    - A no-op item keeps every value, including created_at.
    - Results come back in input order, including unchanged items.
20. **R64** A replay "makes no further state changes". Create with K, cancel, replay K: 200 with the original body. The booking must still be cancelled and the slot still free.
21. **R55** "same key with the same body on a different path ... must succeed normally". K on /reservations, then K on /reservation-moves: 201.
22. **R61** "key order and whitespace do not matter". The same body with reordered keys must give 200, not 409.
23. **R52** "Plaintext password storage is not permitted." No seeded or signup password may appear in GET /_test/export.
24. **R92** PATCH "Validation is identical to POST /reservations". The original must be unchanged after each of these:
    - 17:00 or 22:00 → 422 outside_opening_hours.
    - A skipped DST time → 422 invalid_local_time.
    - party_size 0, "4" or true → 422 validation_failed.
    - An offset in starts_at_local → 422.
    - table_id 5 → 400. A body of `{bad` → 400.
25. **R93** The cutoff is "measured against the current start time". A booking far from its start may be PATCHed into the cutoff window or into the past: 200.

# Tablekeeper — Stage 1: reservations

This stage defines the initial service and its API.

Build from the supplied requirements. Source code, API documentation and schemas from
existing products in this domain must not be used.

## 1. Scope

Diners can search restaurant availability, book a table and receive a confirmation
reference. They can cancel or amend their bookings, including changing several bookings
together. Each restaurant has its own table capacities, opening hours and cancellation policy.
Only the HTTP API is required.

Two `confirmed` reservations must never occupy the same table at overlapping times,
including during concurrent requests. Occupancy is the half-open interval
`[starts_at, starts_at + reservation_duration)`. A 90-minute booking at 19:00 therefore
does not overlap a booking starting at 20:30. Retries and rejected requests must not
create duplicate or partial bookings.

## 2. Delivery and deployment

Deliver an HTTP service, a `Dockerfile` and a `RUN.md` with a command that builds and
starts the service without manual setup. Language, framework and storage are unrestricted.
A `docker-compose.yml` is optional.

The submission is a containerized HTTP service, not a Python package. Python is not
required in the implementation. TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java, Python and any
other language are equally valid. The harness builds the submitted `Dockerfile`, starts
the resulting image and tests only its HTTP behavior; it does not import or execute the
submission's source files on the judge host.

The image must run on its own with `-e PORT=<port>` and a port mapping. Runtime networking
has no outbound access. All runtime dependencies, initialization and seed data must work
within that single container. Compose configuration is not used to start the service.

### Resource limits

The service must operate within these limits:

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 2 vCPU |
| Memory | 2 GiB |
| Start to first healthy response | 60 s |
| Concurrent requests | up to 50 in flight |
| Per-request timeout | 5 s (10 s for `POST /_test/reset`) |
| Outbound network | available during `docker build`, **none at run time** |
| Disk | ephemeral; state need not survive a container restart |

Runtime assets and dependencies must be included in the image. This includes fonts,
scripts and stylesheets; external services are unavailable at runtime.

## 3. Runtime contract

### 3.1 Listening

Listen on `0.0.0.0` using the `PORT` environment variable, default `8080`.

### 3.2 Health

```http
GET /health  ->  200  {"status": "ok"}
```

Return 200 once the service and its data store can serve requests, within 60 seconds
of container start. Non-200 responses are permitted before the service is ready.

### 3.3 Reset and seed

```http
POST /_test/reset
Content-Type: application/json

{ ...fixture... }

->  204 No Content
```

Replace all service state with the fixture in the request body (§4). When reset returns
204, subsequent requests must see only that fixture. Repeated resets are supported.
This test endpoint must be enabled in the delivered image and requires no authentication.

### 3.4 Conventions

- Requests and responses are `application/json; charset=utf-8`.
- Timestamps in responses are RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, e.g. `2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00`.
- Unknown fields in a request body are ignored, never an error.
- Unknown query parameters are ignored.
- IDs are opaque strings of at most 64 characters. Their format is yours. This limit
  also applies to IDs supplied in reset fixtures.

## 4. Model

Restaurants and tables are supplied through `POST /_test/reset` only. Restaurant and
table creation endpoints are out of scope.

| Field | On | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `timezone` | Restaurant | IANA zone name, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. All of the restaurant's times are local to this |
| `slot_minutes` | Restaurant | Bookings start on a grid of this many minutes from opening time |
| `reservation_duration_minutes` | Restaurant | How long every reservation occupies its table |
| `cancellation_cutoff_minutes` | Restaurant | A booking cannot be cancelled or changed within this many minutes of its start |
| `opening_hours` | Restaurant | Per weekday. A day with no entry is closed |
| `capacity` | Table | Maximum party size |

### Fixture format

```json
{
  "users": [
    { "id": "u_ada", "email": "ada@example.com",
      "password": "correct horse", "display_name": "Ada" }
  ],
  "restaurants": [
    {
      "id": "r_anker",
      "name": "Zum Anker",
      "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
      "slot_minutes": 30,
      "reservation_duration_minutes": 90,
      "cancellation_cutoff_minutes": 120,
      "opening_hours": [
        { "weekday": "thu", "opens": "18:00", "closes": "23:00" },
        { "weekday": "fri", "opens": "18:00", "closes": "23:30" }
      ],
      "tables": [
        { "id": "t_1", "label": "1", "capacity": 2 },
        { "id": "t_2", "label": "2", "capacity": 4 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "reservations": []
}
```

- `weekday` is one of `mon tue wed thu fri sat sun`.
- `opens` and `closes` are local `HH:MM`, 24-hour. `closes` is always later than `opens` on the
  same local day — opening hours never cross midnight.
- Seeded users must be able to log in with the given password immediately.
- `reservations` may seed confirmed bookings, with the same fields as a `POST /reservations`
  body plus `id`, `reference` and `user_id`.

Fixtures may use any calendar date. A booking must not be rejected solely because its
start is in the past; the cancellation and amendment cutoff rules still apply.

## 5. Errors

Every 4xx and 5xx response carries this body:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "table_unavailable", "message": "human readable, any wording" } }
```

Use the specified HTTP status and `code`. The human-readable `message` may use any wording.
Endpoint-specific errors are listed with each endpoint.

| Status | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `malformed_request` | Unparseable body, or a field of the wrong JSON type |
| 400 | `missing_idempotency_key` | Required `Idempotency-Key` header absent or empty |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token |
| 403 | `forbidden` | Authenticated, but not permitted to touch this resource |
| 404 | `not_found` | No such resource, or not visible to this caller |
| 409 | `idempotency_key_reuse` | Key already used by this caller with a different request body |
| 422 | `validation_failed` | A required field or query parameter is missing, or a stated rule is violated with no more specific code |

A field of the correct JSON type with an invalid format or out-of-range value gives
422 `validation_failed`, unless an endpoint specifies a different error. This includes
invalid dates, negative counts and values exceeding a stated maximum or length. In addition:

- Endpoint-specific field rules take precedence: invalid `party_size` values (including strings
  and booleans) and `starts_at_local` strings that are not a bare local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` are
  422 `validation_failed`. Other wrong JSON types follow the rule below.
- An integer-valued **query parameter** is written as plain decimal digits: `1e9`, `4.0` and `+4`
  are 422 `validation_failed` whatever their numeric value.
- Reserve 400 `malformed_request` for a body that does not parse or a field of the wrong type.

Shared ranges, enforced on every endpoint that takes them:

| Field | Valid | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | 1 to 255 characters | 422 `validation_failed` |

Requests must not produce 5xx responses, including under concurrent load.

## 6. Authentication

Authentication supports signup and login. Email verification, password reset, refresh
tokens and role-management endpoints are out of scope. Permissions specified elsewhere
in these requirements still apply.

```http
POST /auth/signup
{ "email": "a@example.com", "password": "correct horse", "display_name": "Ada" }

->  201  { "user_id": "u_1", "display_name": "Ada", "token": "..." }
```

```http
POST /auth/login
{ "email": "a@example.com", "password": "correct horse" }

->  200  { "user_id": "u_1", "display_name": "Ada", "token": "..." }
```

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| Email already registered | 409 `email_taken` |
| Password shorter than 8 characters | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `email` not of the form `local@domain` | 422 `validation_failed` |
| Wrong password or unknown email on login | 401 `unauthenticated` |

Every other endpoint requires a bearer token, except `/health`, `/_test/reset`, the two above, and
the three public endpoints named at the top of §8 — `GET /restaurants`, `GET /restaurants/{id}` and
`GET /availability`:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Tokens do not expire. An account may have multiple valid tokens and concurrent sessions.

Passwords must be stored using a password-hashing function such as bcrypt, scrypt or
Argon2, or an equivalent. Plaintext password storage is not permitted.

## 7. Idempotency

Two write paths require an idempotency key: **`POST /reservations`** (§8) and
**`POST /reservation-moves`** (§11).

```http
Idempotency-Key: <client-chosen string, 1..255 characters>
```

The key is scoped to **the authenticated user**. Two different users may use the same key string
with no interaction between them.

A replay means the same user sending the **same method, the same path and the same body**. The
same key with the same body on a different path is a different request, not a replay, and must
succeed normally.

After the body has been parsed as a JSON object and the caller authenticated, idempotency
is resolved before endpoint-specific field validation or current-resource checks. Thus a
used key with a different JSON body returns `409 idempotency_key_reuse` even when that new
body would otherwise be invalid.

| Situation | Response |
|---|---|
| Header absent or empty | 400 `missing_idempotency_key` |
| First use of the key | The normal response, **201** |
| Replay: same key, same body | **200**, body identical to the original response as a JSON value |
| Same key, different body | 409 `idempotency_key_reuse` |
| Key reused after the original request failed with 4xx | Treated as a first use |

"Same body" means the same JSON value after parsing — key order and whitespace do not matter.

For concurrent identical requests with an unused key, exactly one returns 201.
The others return 200 with the same body. The operation takes effect only once.

A successful replay returns the original response, even after the resource changes or
is cancelled. It makes no further state changes.

## 8. API

`GET /restaurants`, `GET /restaurants/{id}` and `GET /availability` are **public** — no bearer
token. Everything else needs one. Diners browse before they sign in.

### `GET /restaurants`

```json
{ "restaurants": [ { "id": "r_anker", "name": "Zum Anker", "timezone": "Europe/Berlin" } ] }
```

### `GET /restaurants/{id}`

The restaurant with its `slot_minutes`, `reservation_duration_minutes`,
`cancellation_cutoff_minutes`, `opening_hours` and `tables`, in the fixture's shape. 404 if
unknown.

### `GET /availability`

```http
GET /availability?restaurant_id=r_anker&date=2026-09-24&party_size=4
```

All three parameters are required; a missing one is 422 `validation_failed`. `date` is a local
calendar date at the restaurant.

```json
{
  "restaurant_id": "r_anker",
  "date": "2026-09-24",
  "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
  "slots": [
    { "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T18:00",
      "starts_at": "2026-09-24T18:00:00+02:00",
      "available_table_ids": ["t_2"] }
  ]
}
```

`starts_at_local` is the full `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` and goes into `POST /reservations` unchanged.

A slot appears for every `slot_minutes` step from `opens` such that
`slot + reservation_duration_minutes <= closes`. `available_table_ids` lists the tables of that
restaurant with `capacity >= party_size` and no overlapping confirmed reservation, in fixture
order. A slot with no available table still appears, with an empty list.

A closed day returns `"slots": []`.

### `POST /reservations`

`Idempotency-Key` is required; see §7.

```http
POST /reservations
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: 2f9c1a...

{ "restaurant_id": "r_anker", "table_id": "t_2",
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00", "party_size": 4 }
```

`starts_at_local` is wall-clock at the restaurant, with no offset and no `Z`. Resolve it against
the restaurant's `timezone`.

```json
201
{
  "reservation_id": "res_7",
  "reference": "K3P7QW",
  "restaurant_id": "r_anker",
  "table_id": "t_2",
  "party_size": 4,
  "status": "confirmed",
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00",
  "starts_at": "2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00",
  "ends_at": "2026-09-24T20:30:00+02:00",
  "created_at": "2026-09-21T11:04:03+00:00"
}
```

`reference` is 6 to 12 characters of `A-Z0-9`, unique across all reservations, and never changes.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| The table is taken for an overlapping interval | 409 `table_unavailable` |
| `starts_at_local` is not on the slot grid | 422 `not_on_slot_grid` |
| Slot outside opening hours, or the reservation would end after `closes` | 422 `outside_opening_hours` |
| `party_size` exceeds the table's `capacity` | 422 `party_exceeds_capacity` |
| `party_size` below 1, or not an integer | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `starts_at_local` is a local time that does not exist (see §9) | 422 `invalid_local_time` |
| Unknown restaurant, unknown table, or the table belongs to another restaurant | 404 `not_found` |

### `GET /reservations`

The caller's reservations, `starts_at` descending, confirmed and cancelled alike.
Return `200` with `{"reservations": [...]}`; each entry has the same shape as the
create response. An empty list is `{"reservations": []}`.

### `GET /reservations/{reference}`

One reservation. **404 if it is not the caller's** — do not leak the existence of other people's
bookings.

### `POST /reservations/{reference}/cancel`

```json
200
{ "reference": "K3P7QW", "status": "cancelled", ... }
```

Frees the table immediately: the next `GET /availability` must offer that slot again.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| Already cancelled | 200 with the current state — cancelling twice is not an error |
| Now is within `cancellation_cutoff_minutes` of `starts_at`, or later | 409 `cutoff_passed` |
| Not the caller's reservation | 404 `not_found` |

### `PATCH /reservations/{reference}`

Change the time, the table or the party size. Any subset of `table_id`, `starts_at_local`,
`party_size`. No idempotency key is required here.

Validation is identical to `POST /reservations`, and the same cutoff rule as cancel applies
(409 `cutoff_passed`), measured against the **current** start time. A cancelled reservation is
409 `reservation_cancelled`. A successful amendment releases the old slot and reserves the
new one together. A failed amendment leaves the original booking and its occupancy unchanged.

`reference` and `reservation_id` survive a change.

## 9. Time and DST

Local dates and times follow the restaurant's `timezone`, including daylight-saving transitions.

**Spring forward.** Local times in the skipped hour do not exist. They never appear in
availability, and booking one is 422 `invalid_local_time`.

**Fall back.** Local times in the repeated hour occur twice. **Always resolve to the first
occurrence — the one before the clocks change.** The slot appears once in availability, and the
second occurrence is not bookable.

`reservation_duration_minutes` is **absolute time**, not wall-clock. A 90-minute reservation
starting at 01:30 on a fall-back night ends 90 real minutes later, and its local `ends_at` will
read 02:00, not 03:00.

The transitions that must be handled:

| Zone | Spring forward | Fall back |
|---|---|---|
| `Europe/Berlin` | 2026-03-29, 02:00 → 03:00 | 2026-10-25, 03:00 → 02:00 |
| `America/New_York` | 2026-03-08, 02:00 → 03:00 | 2026-11-01, 02:00 → 01:00 |

Offsets must follow the IANA rules for the specified zone and date.

## 10. Export and import

The service must support `GET /_test/export` and `POST /_test/import`. Like reset, these
are unauthenticated test endpoints.
Exports may contain credentials and session tokens; handle them as private test artifacts.
Return 200 from export with a JSON object containing `track: "tablekeeper"`,
`format_version: 1` and `state` (an implementation-defined JSON object). The state format
is opaque to the caller and must be accepted unchanged by import.

Import takes that entire object and atomically replaces the service's state, returning
204. It must accept an unchanged export produced by this service. No dependency on the
source process, files, volume, port or network address is allowed. Import is replacement,
not merge; repeating it restores the exported state without duplicating anything. Invalid
JSON follows §5; missing fields, wrong track/version or an invalid state give 422
`validation_failed` without changing the destination. Test control calls have a 10-second
timeout. Export is an atomic, read-only snapshot; subsequent source writes do not change it.

Preserve accounts and hashed-password login, existing bearer tokens, fixture configuration,
reservations, references, all completed idempotent request bodies and original responses.
Identities, statuses and timestamps must not be regenerated. Failed request keys remain
reusable. Existing receipts, references, tokens and retries must remain valid after import;
replacing the state with a fresh fixture does not satisfy this requirement. Import removes
all previous destination data and credentials. Reset continues to clear all state, including
imported state. State need not survive an abrupt container restart.

## 11. Atomic reservation moves

A diner may change several bookings in one request.

`POST /reservation-moves` requires authentication and an idempotency key. Body:

```json
{"moves": [{"reference": "BOOK01", "table_id": "t_2"},
           {"reference": "BOOK02", "table_id": "t_1"}]}
```

`moves` contains 1..8 objects with distinct string references. Invalid shape or duplicate
references gives 422 `validation_failed`. Every booking must belong to the caller and the
same restaurant. Unknown/another owner's reference gives 404 `not_found`; different
restaurants give 422 `validation_failed`. No token gives 401.

Each item accepts the ordinary PATCH fields `table_id`, `starts_at_local`, `party_size`;
omitted fields retain their current values and unknown fields are ignored. The booking's
identity, owner and creation time never change. Cancelled bookings give 409
`reservation_cancelled`. Each booking's existing cutoff applies. Non-occupancy errors use
ordinary amendment codes and take precedence in input order, with cutoff errors preceding
other changes for that booking. An overlap among resulting bookings or with an unlisted
booking gives 409 `table_unavailable`. Unchanged listed bookings retain their occupancy.

Either every move commits or nothing changes: occupancy, reservation records and retry
keys. On success return 201 with `{"reservations": [...]}` in input order, including
unchanged items.
Replays return that original response with 200, even after amendments or cancellations.
No-op moves retain all existing values. Export/import preserves successful batch receipts
as well as the resulting bookings. No batch UI is required.

# Tablekeeper stage 1: gap list (requirements the shipped checks do not fully exercise)

Seat: spec-auditor. Ledger: `audit/ledger-stage-1.md` (R1–R136, A1–A10).
Ranked by how easily an implementation would get it wrong. Each item lists the quote, what a violation looks like, and a test scenario.
"Default world" here means one Berlin restaurant open 18:00–23:00, a 30-minute grid, 90-minute duration, 120-minute cutoff, tables of capacity 2, 4 and 6, and two users.

## Tier 1: very likely to be wrong

1. **R95, PATCH conflicts with itself.** "A successful amendment releases the old slot and reserves the new one together."
   Violation: moving 19:00 → 19:30 on the same table returns 409 table_unavailable.
   Scenario: book table B at 19:00. PATCH `starts_at_local` to 19:30 → 200, and availability no longer shows B at 19:00 but does block 19:30–20:30.
2. **R130/R129, a move batch swap and its overlaps.** The spec's own example swaps two tables; "An overlap among resulting bookings or with an unlisted booking gives 409".
   Violation: the swap returns 409 because each move is checked one at a time against the old state. Or two listed bookings moved onto the same table and time both commit.
   Scenarios: (a) A on t_1, B on t_2 at the same time; one batch swaps them → 201, and both tables stay occupied. (b) A batch moving A and B onto the same table at overlapping times → 409, and nothing changes. (c) A batch moving A onto a table held by an unlisted booking C → 409.
3. **R132/R5/R96, all or nothing.** "Either every move commits or nothing changes: occupancy, reservation records and retry keys." / "A failed amendment leaves the original booking and its occupancy unchanged."
   Violation: the first item is applied before the second fails, or a failed PATCH has already released the old slot.
   Scenarios: a batch [valid move of A, B → off-grid time] → 422 not_on_slot_grid; A is unchanged and its old slot is still occupied. Then reuse the same key with a corrected body → 201 (the key was not consumed). For PATCH: a change onto a taken table → 409, and the original slot is still blocked in availability.
4. **R56, idempotency is checked before validation.** "a used key with a different JSON body returns 409 idempotency_key_reuse even when that new body would otherwise be invalid."
   Violation: 422 or 404 is returned instead of 409.
   Scenario: create with key K. Then send key K with `party_size: 0`, or an unknown restaurant → 409 idempotency_key_reuse.
5. **R60/R116, a failed key is reusable.** "Key reused after the original request failed with 4xx: Treated as a first use."
   Violation: the 4xx response is cached and replayed, or a different body gets 409.
   Scenario: key K on an off-grid time → 422. Key K again with a valid, *different* body → 201. Also after an import (R116).
6. **R62/R2, concurrent identical requests.** "exactly one returns 201. The others return 200 with the same body. The operation takes effect only once."
   Violation: several 201s, a 409 table_unavailable for the losers, a 409 key reuse, or a 5xx.
   Scenario: 20 parallel identical POSTs with one key from one user → exactly one 201 and nineteen 200s with identical bodies; GET /reservations shows exactly one booking.
7. **R2, concurrency on every write path.** "including during concurrent requests"
   Violation: a race on PATCH, cancel-and-rebook or moves double-books a table.
   Scenarios: 50 in flight. (a) Many users PATCH different bookings onto one free table and time → exactly one 200. (b) One user cancels while others create on the freed slot → at most one confirmed booking per interval. (c) Overlapping but non-identical starts (19:00 and 19:30) raced on one table → exactly one 201. (d) Concurrent move batches touching the same tables.
8. **R28, past dates are bookable.** "A booking must not be rejected solely because its start is in the past"
   Violation: a 422 for a past date.
   Scenario: POST a valid on-grid booking dated a few weeks ago → 201. Cancel or PATCH it → 409 cutoff_passed (R29).
9. **R99, skipped times are not offered.** "Local times in the skipped hour do not exist. They never appear in availability"
   Violation: a 02:00 or 02:30 slot on 2026-03-29 in Berlin (2026-03-08 in New York), possibly with a shifted offset.
   Scenario: a restaurant open 00:00–23:30 in each zone; availability on the spring-forward date has no 02:xx slots, and the 01:30 and 03:00 slots carry the right offsets.
10. **R104, overlap uses absolute instants on a fall-back night.** It follows from "duration is absolute time" and from R1.
    Violation: comparing wall-clock times lets 01:30 (ending 02:00+01:00) and 02:00 (+02:00) coexist.
    Scenario: Berlin 2026-10-25, table B. Book 01:30 → ends `02:00:00+01:00`. Book 02:00 on B → 409 table_unavailable, because the first occurrence of 02:00 falls inside the 01:30 booking.
11. **R20, the grid is anchored at opening time.** "Bookings start on a grid of this many minutes from opening time"
    Violation: a grid based on midnight or the hour; 18:15 is rejected or 18:30 is offered.
    Scenario: opens 18:15, closes 22:00, slot 30, duration 90 → slots 18:15, 18:45 … 20:15, 20:30 is off-grid (422 not_on_slot_grid). Also slot 45 with duration 60.
12. **R119, IDs after a seed or import.** It follows from "unique across all reservations".
    Violation: a counter-based `reservation_id` or reference restarts after reset or import and collides with a seeded or imported one. Lookups then return the wrong booking.
    Scenarios: seed a reservation with id `res_1` and a reference; create a new one → a different `reservation_id` and reference. Export, create, import, create → no collision with any imported ID or reference.

## Tier 2: likely to be wrong

13. **R114/R113, export and import keep idempotency and logins.** "Preserve ... all completed idempotent request bodies and original responses" / "accounts and hashed-password login"
    Scenario: create with key K. Export, reset, import. Key K with the same body → 200 and the original body. Key K with a different body → 409. Login with the password → 200.
14. **R111, a bad import changes nothing.** "missing fields, wrong track/version or an invalid state give 422 `validation_failed` without changing the destination." / "Invalid JSON follows §5".
    Scenarios: import `{}`, `track: "other"`, `format_version: 2`, `state: "garbage"`, `state: {}` → 422 each, and existing bookings are still readable afterwards. Import of `{not json` → 400 malformed_request.
15. **R117/R118/R110, replacement semantics.** "Import removes all previous destination data and credentials." / "Reset continues to clear all state, including imported state." / "repeating it restores the exported state without duplicating anything".
    Scenarios: sign up X on the destination, then import → X's token gives 401, X's login gives 401, and X's email can be signed up again. Import the same snapshot twice → the list is not duplicated. Import, then reset → imported users and bookings are gone.
16. **R11, reset clears everything.** "Replace all service state with the fixture"
    Violation: signup accounts, old tokens, bookings or idempotency records survive a reset.
    Scenario: sign up X and book with key K. Reset to a fixture without X → X's token gives 401 and X's login gives 401. A seeded user reusing key K with the same body → 201, not a replay.
17. **R121–R128, move-batch validation.** "1..8 objects with distinct string references", "Unknown/another owner's reference gives 404", "different restaurants give 422", "Cancelled bookings give 409", "Each booking's existing cutoff applies", "No token gives 401", key required.
    Scenarios: 0 items or 9 items → 422. A duplicate reference → 422. A numeric reference → 422. Another user's reference → 404. Bookings in two restaurants → 422. One cancelled → 409 reservation_cancelled. One inside the cutoff → 409 cutoff_passed. No token → 401. No key → 400 missing_idempotency_key. An item with a party over capacity → 422 party_exceeds_capacity. In every case, nothing changes.
18. **R128, error precedence inside a batch.** "take precedence in input order, with cutoff errors preceding other changes for that booking"
    Scenario: [A with an off-grid time, B cancelled] → 422 not_on_slot_grid. [B cancelled, A off-grid] → 409 reservation_cancelled. A inside the cutoff with an off-grid time → 409 cutoff_passed.
19. **R134/R125/R135/R133, batch receipts.** "Replays return that original response with 200, even after amendments or cancellations." / "identity, owner and creation time never change" / "No-op moves retain all existing values" / "in input order, including unchanged items".
    Scenarios: run a batch, cancel one of the bookings, replay → 200 with an identical body. A no-op item (reference only) → returned unchanged with the same `created_at`. Results come back in input order rather than sorted.
20. **R64/R4, a replay makes no further state changes.** "It makes no further state changes."
    Violation: a replay after cancel re-confirms the booking or re-occupies the table.
    Scenario: create with key K, cancel, replay K → 200 with the original confirmed body. GET by reference still says cancelled, and the slot is still free.
21. **R55, the same key on a different path.** "The same key with the same body on a different path is a different request, not a replay, and must succeed normally."
    Scenario: use key K on POST /reservations, then on POST /reservation-moves → 201 (not 409 or 200).
22. **R61, "same body" is JSON-value equality.** "key order and whitespace do not matter."
    Scenario: replay the same body with its keys reordered and extra whitespace → 200, not 409.
23. **R52, password hashing.** "Plaintext password storage is not permitted."
    Scenario: GET /_test/export; neither the seeded password nor a signup password appears anywhere in the JSON.
24. **R92, PATCH validation matches create in full.** "Validation is identical to `POST /reservations`"
    Scenarios: PATCH to 17:00 or 22:00 → 422 outside_opening_hours. PATCH to a skipped DST time → 422 invalid_local_time. `party_size: 0`, `"4"` or `true` → 422 validation_failed. `starts_at_local: "…+02:00"` → 422. `table_id: 5` → 400 malformed_request. A body of `{bad` → 400. In every case, the original is unchanged.
25. **R93, the cutoff is measured against the current start.** "measured against the **current** start time"
    Scenario: a booking far outside the cutoff may be PATCHed to a time inside it (or a past time) → 200. The reverse, a booking inside the cutoff, cannot be moved later → 409.

## Tier 3: plausible mistakes

26. **R39, party_size as a boolean.** "invalid `party_size` values (including strings and booleans) ... are 422"
    Scenario: `party_size: true` on POST, PATCH and moves → 422 validation_failed, never 201 and never 400.
27. **R33/R32, wrong JSON types and non-object bodies.** "a field of the wrong JSON type" → 400. "Other wrong JSON types follow the rule below."
    Scenarios: `restaurant_id: 5` or `table_id: true` → 400 malformed_request. `starts_at_local: 1900` → 400. A body of `[]`, `"x"`, `null` → 400. Signup or login with `password: 123` → 400.
28. **R37, a missing required body field.** "A required field ... is missing" → 422.
    Scenario: POST /reservations without `table_id` (or `starts_at_local`, or `party_size`) → 422 validation_failed. Signup without `display_name` or `password` → 422.
29. **R42, Idempotency-Key length.** "1 to 255 characters" else 422.
    Scenario: a 256-char key → 422 validation_failed. A 255-char key → 201.
30. **R34, an empty key.** "absent or empty" → 400 missing_idempotency_key.
    Scenario: `Idempotency-Key:` with an empty value → 400.
31. **R35, a malformed bearer token.** "Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token" → 401.
    Scenario: `Authorization: Basic abc`, `Authorization: Bearer` with nothing after it, `Authorization: Token x` → 401 unauthenticated.
32. **R50, write endpoints need a token.** "Every other endpoint requires a bearer token"
    Scenario: POST /reservations, cancel, PATCH and POST /reservation-moves without a token → 401, never 400 or 404.
33. **R51, multiple tokens.** "An account may have multiple valid tokens and concurrent sessions."
    Scenario: log in twice; both tokens work. The signup token still works after a later login.
34. **R23, per-weekday hours.** "Per weekday. A day with no entry is closed"
    Scenario: Thursday 18:00–23:00 and Friday 18:00–23:30. On Friday 22:00 is a slot and bookable; on Thursday it is not (422 outside_opening_hours).
35. **R79, booking on a closed day.** "Slot outside opening hours" → 422 outside_opening_hours.
    Scenario: POST for a weekday with no entry → 422 outside_opening_hours (not 404, not a 201).
36. **R40, impossible values in starts_at_local.** "not a bare local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`" and invalid dates → 422.
    Scenario: `2026-02-30T19:00`, `2026-09-24T24:00`, `2026-09-24 19:00`, `2026-09-24T9:00` → 422 validation_failed.
37. **R70, fixture order.** "in fixture order"
    Scenario: tables listed as [t_9 (cap 4), t_1 (cap 4)] → `available_table_ids` is `["t_9","t_1"]`, not sorted.
38. **R101/R82/R100, New York DST.** "The transitions that must be handled: America/New_York"
    Scenarios: 2026-11-01 01:30 → `-04:00`, and the slot appears once. 2026-03-08 02:30 → 422 invalid_local_time, absent from availability. 2026-03-08 03:00 → `-04:00`.
39. **R103/R105/R106, offsets on transition days.** "Offsets must follow the IANA rules"
    Scenarios: Berlin 2026-10-25 01:30 booking → `ends_at` = `2026-10-25T02:00:00+01:00`. Berlin 2026-03-29 01:00 → `ends_at` `03:30:00+02:00`. Availability `starts_at` on both days carries the right offset per slot.
40. **R18, ID limit across all fixture IDs.** "IDs are opaque strings of at most 64 characters ... also applies to IDs supplied in reset fixtures"
    Scenarios: a 65-char restaurant, table or reservation ID → reset 422. Exactly 64 chars → 204, and that ID is usable in a booking.
41. **R27, seeded reservation fields.** "with the same fields as a `POST /reservations` body plus `id`, `reference` and `user_id`"
    Scenario: GET by the seeded reference → `reservation_id` equals the seeded `id`, with correct `starts_at`/`ends_at` offsets and a `created_at`.
42. **R66, restaurant detail in the fixture's shape.** "in the fixture's shape"
    Scenario: GET /restaurants/{id} → returns `id`, `name`, `timezone`, the opening_hours entries with weekday/opens/closes exactly as seeded, and tables with `id`/`label`/`capacity` in fixture order.
43. **R107/R108/R112, export envelope.** "`track: "tablekeeper"`, `format_version: 1` and `state`"; unauthenticated; "subsequent source writes do not change it"
    Scenario: GET /_test/export with no token → 200 with the three fields. Create a booking, then import the earlier export → the new booking is gone.
44. **R46/R47/R44/R45, auth details.** Email taken for an API signup (not just a seeded user). An 8-character password is accepted. Signup and login return a `user_id`, and it is the same for both.
45. **R84/R86/R15, response shapes.** List entries, cancel and PATCH responses carry the full create shape with offset timestamps. An empty list is `{"reservations": []}`.
46. **R87, a freed table can be rebooked.** "Frees the table immediately"
    Scenario: cancel, then another user books the same table and time → 201.
47. **R16, unknown fields elsewhere.** "Unknown fields in a request body are ignored"
    Scenario: extra fields on signup, login, PATCH, move items and the reset fixture → still succeed.
48. **R14, content type.** Responses carry `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` (a 204 has no body).
49. **R31, error message.** Every error body has `error.message` as a string.
50. **R8/R43, load.** 50 in flight, each under 5 s, with no 5xx.
51. **R9, default port.** With PORT unset, the service listens on 8080.

## Ambiguities (proposed readings in ledger A1–A10)
A1 off-grid and outside hours → outside_opening_hours. A2 create error precedence 404 → 422 → 409. A3 401 before 400 missing key. A4 cancel twice inside the cutoff → 200. A5 cancelled and past cutoff on PATCH → reservation_cancelled. A6 public endpoint with a bad token → 200. A7 `moves` not a list → 422. A8 email compared case-insensitively. A9 DST closing check uses absolute instants. A10 a fixture with overlapping or invalid seeded bookings → reset 422.

Single-container HTTP service (Python 3.12, standard library only; `tzdata` is installed at build time).


=== FULL SPECIFICATION, STAGE 1 ===
# Tablekeeper — Stage 1: reservations

This stage defines the initial service and its API.

Build from the supplied requirements. Source code, API documentation and schemas from
existing products in this domain must not be used.

## 1. Scope

Diners can search restaurant availability, book a table and receive a confirmation
reference. They can cancel or amend their bookings, including changing several bookings
together. Each restaurant has its own table capacities, opening hours and cancellation policy.
Only the HTTP API is required.

Two `confirmed` reservations must never occupy the same table at overlapping times,
including during concurrent requests. Occupancy is the half-open interval
`[starts_at, starts_at + reservation_duration)`. A 90-minute booking at 19:00 therefore
does not overlap a booking starting at 20:30. Retries and rejected requests must not
create duplicate or partial bookings.

## 2. Delivery and deployment

Deliver an HTTP service, a `Dockerfile` and a `RUN.md` with a command that builds and
starts the service without manual setup. Language, framework and storage are unrestricted.
A `docker-compose.yml` is optional.

The submission is a containerized HTTP service, not a Python package. Python is not
required in the implementation. TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java, Python and any
other language are equally valid. The harness builds the submitted `Dockerfile`, starts
the resulting image and tests only its HTTP behavior; it does not import or execute the
submission's source files on the judge host.

The image must run on its own with `-e PORT=<port>` and a port mapping. Runtime networking
has no outbound access. All runtime dependencies, initialization and seed data must work
within that single container. Compose configuration is not used to start the service.

### Resource limits

The service must operate within these limits:

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 2 vCPU |
| Memory | 2 GiB |
| Start to first healthy response | 60 s |
| Concurrent requests | up to 50 in flight |
| Per-request timeout | 5 s (10 s for `POST /_test/reset`) |
| Outbound network | available during `docker build`, **none at run time** |
| Disk | ephemeral; state need not survive a container restart |

Runtime assets and dependencies must be included in the image. This includes fonts,
scripts and stylesheets; external services are unavailable at runtime.

## 3. Runtime contract

### 3.1 Listening

Listen on `0.0.0.0` using the `PORT` environment variable, default `8080`.

### 3.2 Health

```http
GET /health  ->  200  {"status": "ok"}
```

Return 200 once the service and its data store can serve requests, within 60 seconds
of container start. Non-200 responses are permitted before the service is ready.

### 3.3 Reset and seed

```http
POST /_test/reset
Content-Type: application/json

{ ...fixture... }

->  204 No Content
```

Replace all service state with the fixture in the request body (§4). When reset returns
204, subsequent requests must see only that fixture. Repeated resets are supported.
This test endpoint must be enabled in the delivered image and requires no authentication.

### 3.4 Conventions

- Requests and responses are `application/json; charset=utf-8`.
- Timestamps in responses are RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, e.g. `2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00`.
- Unknown fields in a request body are ignored, never an error.
- Unknown query parameters are ignored.
- IDs are opaque strings of at most 64 characters. Their format is yours. This limit
  also applies to IDs supplied in reset fixtures.

## 4. Model

Restaurants and tables are supplied through `POST /_test/reset` only. Restaurant and
table creation endpoints are out of scope.

| Field | On | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `timezone` | Restaurant | IANA zone name, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. All of the restaurant's times are local to this |
| `slot_minutes` | Restaurant | Bookings start on a grid of this many minutes from opening time |
| `reservation_duration_minutes` | Restaurant | How long every reservation occupies its table |
| `cancellation_cutoff_minutes` | Restaurant | A booking cannot be cancelled or changed within this many minutes of its start |
| `opening_hours` | Restaurant | Per weekday. A day with no entry is closed |
| `capacity` | Table | Maximum party size |

### Fixture format

```json
{
  "users": [
    { "id": "u_ada", "email": "ada@example.com",
      "password": "correct horse", "display_name": "Ada" }
  ],
  "restaurants": [
    {
```

|---|---|

|---|---|

Local dates and times follow the restaurant's `timezone`, including daylight-saving transitions.

**Spring forward.** Local times in the skipped hour do not exist. They never appear in
availability, and booking one is 422 `invalid_local_time`.

**Fall back.** Local times in the repeated hour occur twice. **Always resolve to the first
occurrence — the one before the clocks change.** The slot appears once in availability, and the
second occurrence is not bookable.

`reservation_duration_minutes` is **absolute time**, not wall-clock. A 90-minute reservation
starting at 01:30 on a fall-back night ends 90 real minutes later, and its local `ends_at` will
read 02:00, not 03:00.

The transitions that must be handled:

| Zone | Spring forward | Fall back |
|---|---|---|
| `Europe/Berlin` | 2026-03-29, 02:00 → 03:00 | 2026-10-25, 03:00 → 02:00 |
| `America/New_York` | 2026-03-08, 02:00 → 03:00 | 2026-11-01, 02:00 → 01:00 |

identity, owner and creation time never change. Cancelled bookings give 409

ordinary amendment codes and take precedence in input order, with cutoff errors preceding
other changes for that booking. An overlap among resulting bookings or with an unlisted
booking gives 409 `table_unavailable`. Unchanged listed bookings retain their occupancy.

keys. On success return 201 with `{"reservations": [...]}` in input order, including
unchanged items.

# Tablekeeper — Stage 1: reservations

This stage defines the initial service and its API.

Build from the supplied requirements. Source code, API documentation and schemas from
existing products in this domain must not be used.

## 1. Scope

Diners can search restaurant availability, book a table and receive a confirmation
reference. They can cancel or amend their bookings, including changing several bookings
together. Each restaurant has its own table capacities, opening hours and cancellation policy.
Only the HTTP API is required.

Two `confirmed` reservations must never occupy the same table at overlapping times,
including during concurrent requests. Occupancy is the half-open interval
`[starts_at, starts_at + reservation_duration)`. A 90-minute booking at 19:00 therefore
does not overlap a booking starting at 20:30. Retries and rejected requests must not
create duplicate or partial bookings.

## 2. Delivery and deployment

Deliver an HTTP service, a `Dockerfile` and a `RUN.md` with a command that builds and
starts the service without manual setup. Language, framework and storage are unrestricted.
A `docker-compose.yml` is optional.

The submission is a containerized HTTP service, not a Python package. Python is not
required in the implementation. TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java, Python and any
other language are equally valid. The harness builds the submitted `Dockerfile`, starts
the resulting image and tests only its HTTP behavior; it does not import or execute the
submission's source files on the judge host.

The image must run on its own with `-e PORT=<port>` and a port mapping. Runtime networking
has no outbound access. All runtime dependencies, initialization and seed data must work
within that single container. Compose configuration is not used to start the service.

The service must operate within these limits:

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 2 vCPU |
| Memory | 2 GiB |
| Start to first healthy response | 60 s |
| Concurrent requests | up to 50 in flight |
| Per-request timeout | 5 s (10 s for `POST /_test/reset`) |
| Outbound network | available during `docker build`, **none at run time** |
| Disk | ephemeral; state need not survive a container restart |
